title: Audit sampling skew impacting per-model usage breakdowns in Console
creator: Maya Chen
description: Symptoms: Several customers reported inconsistent per-model token charges in Console charts compared to raw billing exports. Low-volume models (long-tail) show amplified deltas after late-event backfills. Charts sometimes display spikes or negative adjustments after backfill jobs run. Impact: incorrect customer-facing per-model breakdowns in Console and downstream billing reconciliation confusion.
investigation_summary: We ran a sampling and ingestion audit across the last 60 days of events for three affected tenants. Findings: (1) The ingest pipeline applies a 1-in-10 sampling step for low-volume shards under heavy load; sampled keys were being upweighted incorrectly in the final aggregation when late events arrived. (2) Rate-limit rejection events were stored in a separate bucket and merged later without consistent source weighting, causing over-attribution to certain model aliases. (3) The backfill job deduplication logic uses event IDs without accounting for event-time vs processing-time ordering, so late-arriving token events for streaming prefix use were double-counted in ~0.7% of windows.
root_cause: A combination of three issues: sampling upweight applied after aggregation rather than at ingest, asynchronous merge of the rate-limit-reject bucket without source provenance, and dedupe logic that assumes monotonic processing time. These interact non-linearly for low-volume models and during backfills, producing the observed chart artifacts.
proposed_changes: 1) Move sampling upweight to the earliest ingest stage so that all downstream aggregations operate on consistently-weighted records. 2) Add provenance tags to rate-limit rejection events (source_shard, ingest_ts, orig_event_ts) and include provenance-aware merge rules. 3) Replace current dedupe heuristic with a time-windowed dedupe that prefers event_time and validates KV cache prefix consistency for streaming tokens. 4) Add compensating backfill job that recomputes final aggregates for affected windows rather than applying incremental patches.
implementation_notes:
- New ingest handler will add __sample_weight and we will fold it into the composite key used by rolling aggregates.
- Backfill recompute job implemented as a Spark job (re-use existing backfill infra) and writes to staging tables before swap.
- Update downstream console caching layer to invalidate per-model caches on swap.
- Required schema change: add 'provenance' map fields in events table (we will encode as flattened columns: provenance_source, provenance_ingest_ts, provenance_event_ts).
- Estimated infra effort: small-schema migrations + 2-week rollout for backfill with canary tenants.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy sampling-weight change to staging and 3 low-traffic tenants for 48 hours, validate aggregate parity with raw billing exports. Phase 2: enable provenance tagging and merge rule update across all ingestion shards, run a small-scale backfill for the last 7 days. Phase 3: run full recompute backfill for affected 60-day window during a 4-hour maintenance window (off-hours). Phase 4: monitor and revert option (ability to swap old aggregates back if delta > 0.5% for any tenant).
acceptance_criteria:
- Console per-model charts match billing exports within 0.2% for a representative set of tenants across traffic percentiles.
- No increase in duplicate token counts post-deploy.
- Backfill recompute completes within the SLA window and cache invalidations propagate without >5 min lag.
- Dashboard for 'backfill delta' shows <0.1% of tenants with >1% delta after final run.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for sample-weight propagation and dedupe window behavior.
- Integration test: ingest synthetic sampled load and late-arrival events; assert final aggregator output equals ground truth.
- End-to-end canary: enable on 3 tenants, compare console charts vs raw billing exports and export CSVs for audit.
- Load test: ensure new provenance columns don't increase ingest tail latency beyond 10%.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- New Grafana panel 'Per-model backfill delta' (per-tenant) with alert if >0.5% tenants exceed 1%.
- Alert on backfill job failures and >10% runtime increase.
- SLO: ingest tail P99 should remain within current baseline +10% during rollout.
